questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code makes batch ingestion idempotent? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
Two simultaneous requests with the same account, key and payload arrive. What happens to the second one?
choices: It receives 409 if the first has not finished, or the replayed 202 if it has
It writes the events again, and duplicates are removed later
It waits on a lock until the first finishes
It receives 422 for a conflicting payload

questions.prompt: The writer raises an exception partway through the first attempt. What is the state for a later retry with the same key?
choices: The key stays claimed and retries get 409 until the TTL expires
The retry replays a stored 500 response
The claim row is removed by abandon, so a retry can start fresh
The retry returns 422 because the fingerprint changed

questions.prompt: Why does fingerprint serialize the payload with sort_keys=True?
choices: To make the SHA-256 digest cryptographically stronger
To make the stored body smaller
So semantically identical payloads with different key order hash the same
